scope: Summarize opt-in Spark timings within conservatively trimmed workload windows.
caveats: Only rows <= 80; includes warmup and any small prefill executions in these windows.
Window assignment uses host/worker wall clocks; post-run SSH bounds fit the trim, but do not prove historical clock stability.
GPU time is a CUDA event interval including wire decode, routing, expert computation, output reduction and possible submission gaps; not isolated kernel busy time.
GPU time overlaps enqueue and wait; these columns must not be added together.
Worker timing begins after connection polling, so excludes time waiting behind another connection.
Rank averages are not request-matched maximums and cannot be subtracted from coordinator stage averages to measure transport latency.
Tracing perturbs timing; these are optimization diagnostics, not release benchmarks.

coordinator.scope: Summarize opt-in serving traces; elapsed stages include scheduler/transport waits.
caveats: Includes benchmark warmup and all three measured samples.
Concurrent lanes overlap; layer times must not be added as end-to-end wall time.
Zero acceptance counts lane rounds, not individual request cycles.
Tracing perturbs throughput; these are optimization diagnostics, not release tables.

findings: Spark ranks 0/1 have 640-wide intermediate slices; ranks 2/3 have 512-wide slices. Wider ranks consistently take longer in this run.
Code C1 mean CUDA interval on rank 0 is 586 us; C8 is 700 us. Topic C1 is 345 us; C8 is 339 us. This is much less growth than coordinator expert-stage elapsed time.

The native local service owns one execution workspace/stream and synchronously executes a connection before polling the next. Cross-connection waiting is outside these worker measurements; it is a plausible contributor to the higher concurrent coordinator expert latency, not directly measured here.
Investigate worker scheduling and kernel throughput together. Concurrent GPU submission alone does not increase available memory bandwidth and needs an end-to-end experiment before adoption.
